newsitem.title: UK: UK Liberals urge one billion stg fuel firms levy.
newsitem.headline: UK Liberals urge one billion stg fuel firms levy.

text.p: The minority Liberal Democrats on Monday called for a one billion stg a year levy to be paid by Britain's gas and electricity companies to fund a national programme of investment in energy conservation.
"This would impact companies' bottom lines, but we believe the industry can well afford it," environment spokesman, Matthew Taylor, told as news conference.
He said the idea was preferable to the windfall profits tax proposed by the opposition Labour Party which would do nothing to cut demand for fuel.
Taylor included the suggestion as part of a "Green Budget" package which he presented to Chancellor of the Exchequer Kenneth Clarke for his consideration.
Industry regulators have resisted setting up an energy conservation programme, claiming that legislation would have to go through parliament before they could impose a levy on firms to fund it.
"Our suspicion is that the Government has not been robust in urging the regulators to take this measure," Taylor said.
He said the scheme could help eight million households improve insulation levels and install efficient central heating over 15 years, and in the process create around 60,000 jobs.
Other proposals included a carbon tax which could be used to cut value added tax (VAT) and employers' national insurance contributions, and a cut of VAT on energy saving materials.

The document also urged Clarke to cut vehicle excise duty on cars below 1500 cc to 10 stg a year from 140 stg, paying for this by raising fuel duty by almost three pence a litre. -- London Newsroom +44 171 5427767
